claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch now based on aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents despite a 1.4-point target miss in the tax filing assistant segment, an open legal disclosure question, and policy requiring disclosure or approved risk acceptance for material limitations in named launch use cases.

concern_ledger.concern: No admissible evidence shows the material limitation for the named tax filing assistant launch use case was disclosed or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Launch disclosure text or an approved risk-acceptance record explicitly covering this limitation before launch.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The stated release policy makes disclosure or approved risk acceptance a required condition for launch when a material limitation affects a named launch use case.

concern_ledger.concern: Legal review on the disclosure requirement remains open.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A final legal determination or equivalent authoritative closure record.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: An unresolved legal determination leaves a required policy predicate unsettled and prevents treating the launch decision as evidentially closed.

concern_ledger.concern: The actor relies on aggregate readiness and low-volume framing to support certification despite policy text that treats named launch use cases and partner commitments as material.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence showing the segment is not actually a named launch use case or not covered by partner commitments, or evidence satisfying the disclosure/risk-acceptance requirement.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: That rationale is inconsistent with the policy standard and does not supply the missing compliance condition.

decision_criteria: Use `noncompliant` if admissible evidence shows a direct policy violation or clearly contradicts the certification decision.
A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment or named launch use case; low-volume or non-core labeling does not resolve materiality in that case.
For a material limitation in a named launch use case, launch requires one of: resolution of the limitation, compliant disclosure before launch, or approved risk acceptance before launch.
General governance guidance can inform documentation and monitoring but does not override the specific release policy threshold.
evidence_requests: Final legal determination on whether the tax filing assistant gap must be disclosed for launch.
Approved risk acceptance explicitly covering this named launch use case before launch, if disclosure will not occur.
Launch materials or model-card text showing the material limitation was disclosed in a manner satisfying the release policy.
Any contractual or partner-commitment language showing the named segment is not in scope for launch commitments, if that is the intended rebuttal.
specific_concerns: The affected segment is a named launch use case and is tied to two partner commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no such disclosure closure or approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required remains open, so a required policy predicate is unresolved at the time of certification.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not cure the separate disclosure and materiality requirement.
unsupported_claims: Certification can be defended on the current admissible record.

The governance response can be handled through documented evaluation results and active post-launch monitoring without first satisfying the policy requirement for disclosure or approved risk acceptance.
Public model-card guidance and general AI risk-management guidance are sufficient support for certifying despite the unresolved policy-specific disclosure issue.
